title: The Tiger, the Brahman, and the Jackal
originalTitle: बाघ, ब्राह्मण और सियार · Bāgh, Brāhmaṇ aur Siyār
place: A road beside a tiger’s cage
note: A new concise adaptation of “The Tiger, the Brahman, and the Jackal,” from Joseph Jacobs’s compilation.

rights.basis: Source edition published in 1892 and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A jackal puzzles over a tiger waiting beside an open cage.
scenes: A tiger begged a passing Brahman to open his cage. “I will be grateful forever,” he promised.
But once free, the tiger stretched and announced that he would eat his rescuer.
The Brahman asked three judges whether this was fair. A tree, a buffalo, and the road each remembered how people had used them badly. All sided with the tiger.
Then a jackal arrived. He listened, frowned, and walked around the cage. “I cannot understand. Was the cage inside the tiger, or the Brahman inside the cage?”
“The tiger was inside!” they cried. The jackal shook his head. “Such a large tiger in this little cage? Show me.”
Impatiently, the tiger stepped back inside and curled himself up.
The jackal slammed the door. “Now I understand perfectly,” he said.
The Brahman thanked him and continued down the road, while the tiger had time to consider the worth of a promise.
